name: Natchez Trace — Lower
subtitle: Jackson to Natchez
description: The most dramatic history on the Trace. Spanish moss, ancient mounds, ghost towns, and the town Grant called too beautiful to burn. Best first self-guided tour in the country.

waypoints.name: Start — Jackson Area
waypoints.description: Northern terminus of the Lower Trace. Your ride begins here — 100 miles of NPS parkway ahead, finishing at the Mississippi bluffs in Natchez.

waypoints.name: Rocky Springs
waypoints.description: A ghost town swallowed by forest. The church built in 1837 still stands in the trees. Free NPS camping with water and bear boxes — one of the best campsites in the South.

waypoints.name: Port Gibson
waypoints.description: The town Ulysses Grant called too beautiful to burn. Antebellum architecture intact, the golden hand church steeple points skyward. Best meal of the trip is here.

waypoints.name: Windsor Ruins
waypoints.description: 23 Corinthian columns standing in a field. All that remains of Mississippi's grandest antebellum mansion after an 1890 fire. One mile off the Trace — worth every pedal stroke.

waypoints.name: Sunken Trace
waypoints.description: The original footpath worn six feet into the earth by centuries of foot traffic — Native American traders, Kaintuck boatmen, Andrew Jackson's army. Stop and walk it.

waypoints.name: Emerald Mound
waypoints.description: Second largest Native American ceremonial mound in the United States. Built around 1400 CE. Eight acres of earth moved by hand. Catch it at sunrise if you can.

waypoints.name: Natchez — The Finish
waypoints.description: You made it. One of the oldest cities on the Mississippi. Bluffs, antebellum mansions, cold drink on a porch. You earned it.

waypoints.name: Collina House — Port Gibson
waypoints.description: Historic B&B in Port Gibson. One of the best overnight stops on the Lower Trace. Book well ahead for spring and fall.

waypoints.name: Monmouth Historic Inn — Natchez
waypoints.description: The finish line in style. Antebellum mansion, 30 acres of grounds, dinner on the veranda. If you're going to splurge anywhere on this trip, splurge here.
